thread:
Eleni: Quick spin-up: I want to capture a distinct follow-up to the admission-phase idea with more focus on policy semantics and cache sharding. High-level: admission runs before scoring and emits a compact verdict. Need to settle hard vs soft admission semantics.
Sam: Define the difference you mean by hard/soft?
Eleni: Hard = route removed; scorer never sees it. Soft = route tagged as 'deprioritized' but still visible to scorer (scorer can still pick if worth it).
Jorge: Soft sounds safer for initial rollout but weaker perf gains. Hard gives clearer SLO benefits.
Priya: Also think about fairness: if admission preempts lower-tier routes, tenant billing/observability must show who was preempted. We can't silently drop routes for charge disputes.
Mei: On cache sharding: resolver keeps a local admission cache keyed by (route_id, tenant_id) with TTL 20s by default. To avoid hot-key thundering we shard cache by route_id % N and use per-shard LRU.
Sam: How do we compute N? static config per region? dynamic?
Mei: Start with static per-region based on CPU cores (e.g., N = max(2, cores/2)). We can later expose dynamic autoscale but that's follow-up.
Eleni: Back to semantics: propose a staged policy: 1) Shadow admission: compute admits but don't enforce. 2) Soft-admit: tag deprioritized. 3) Hard-admit: enforce removal. Move through stages after canary.
Jorge: For scoring fairness and determinism, we must ensure scorer sees candidate ordering unaffected by admission (unless hard-admit). For hard-admit, scorer input is reduced; for soft-admit include a deterministic bias factor in scorer for deprioritized routes.
Priya: We need a canonical list of admission predicates. Initial set: region_allowlist, tenant_tier_min, model_family_compat, explicit_maintenance_flag, hard_quota_exceeded. Make them composable.
Sam: Predicate language: simplest is prefix boolean list evaluated left-to-right. That lets us emit 'first-failed' reason which keeps explain payload tiny.
Eleni: Good. For explainability: emit up to 2 rejection entries per request, each entry small: route_id, code (short), and predicate_idx. If preemption happened at tenant level, set preempted_snapshot: a 1-line summary string. Keep default off.
Mei: Add a compact code registry like RM (region_mismatch), TT (tier_too_low), MF (model_family_mismatch), MQ (maintenance_quota). Store the registry in proto/registry rather than strings.
Jorge: Implementation boundary thought: admission lives in resolver service. Resolver returns a CandidateEnvelope per request: candidate_ids CSV string, admission_summary CSV string. No nested JSONs in the wire proto so it's cheap.
Sam: Example proto-ish shape (text):
candidates: "r1,r2,r3"
admit_summary: "r4:RM:1;r5:TT:3"
(where each item is route:code:predicate_index)
Priya: That keeps SDK changes minimal. We'll need parser helpers in client libraries.
Eleni: Safety nets: quality-preserve rule. If admission would remove all routes above quality threshold Q, keep top-quality route. This avoids cost-first regressions.
Jorge: How do we compute quality efficiently? Precompute per-route-family quality score, stored with route metadata in cache. Cheap lookup.
Mei: On cache invalidation: metadata changes (tier bump, region maintenance) should emit a resolver invalidation event. We'll subscribe resolver instances to a small fanout channel; these invalidations are rare.
Sam: Observability: new metrics: admit_total, admit_reject_by_code, preempted_count, admit_latency_ms_histogram, admit_skipped_count. Also console columns as Priya mentioned earlier.
Priya: Add audit log entry when hard-admit removes a route that was active for a tenant in past 24h; this helps postmortems/billing. Audit entries should be rate-limited.
Eleni: Rollout plan: shadow for 72h regionally + sim harness check for candidate sizes [10,50,200] with synthetic traffic shape. Then soft-admit canary for 24h with telemetry checks, then hard-admit at 1% ramp.
Jorge: Rollback conditions: admit_reject_rate > X, p95 latency regression > 5% for scoring-critical routes, fallback_rate > 0.5% absolute, quality_eval_regression > threshold. Define X = 30% as starting point but tune in canary.
Mei: Escape hatch: if admission runtime exceeds 2ms or if cache error rate > 0.5% for window, mark request as admission_skipped and emit admit_skipped metric.
Sam: Testing: unit tests for predicate ordering, sim for large candidate sets, integration tests with scorer to validate soft-admit bias effect.
Priya: Documentation: small SDK note, console telemetry guide, and a runbook for ops. I'll draft the SDK snippet and console columns.
Eleni: Ownership: I'll write the addendum with examples and attach the predicate registry. Mei will own resolver impl details, Sam will update sim harness, Jorge will add dashboards, Priya docs. Ops-bot: perf run #1428 completed: admission sim (10/50/200 candidates): avg admit latency 0.9ms, 99th 3.1ms, p95 overall latency improvement 5.8% for hard-admit at 50 candidates.
Jorge: Nice numbers. One more question: ties when two routes have same score but one was soft-deprioritized. Determinism rule?
Eleni: Deterministic tie-breaker: prefer non-deprioritized; then route_id lexicographic. Documented and unit-tested.
Sam: I'll add a quick benchmark in sim to show hard vs soft trade-offs on quality/latency/cost.
Priya: And I'll add a client compatibility note: old resolvers (no admit_summary) -> treat as all admitted. New resolver -> clients should tolerate absent admit_summary gracefully.
Eleni: OK. I'll circulate the addendum with a checklist and a small proto text example. Aim to post by tomorrow morning. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
